keyArticles.title: 2nd Side Formula
keyArticles.body: Question What is the 2 nd side formula? Answer Healthy Usage Healthy Usage is a check to see if both sides are being used once a certain number of items come through. It starts with checking if there have been 36/38 (breakfast/regular menu) items in a quarter hour period. Once that threshold is met, then at least 20% of the items need to be on each side to count as Healthy Usage. The :15 result will be either 0% or 100% (if threshold met) If the threshold is met for a full hour but only 3 of the 4 quarter hours meet 20% on each side, the hour would show as 75%. The same averaging would calculate for the full day information. If a quarter hour does not meet 36/38 total items sold, it will display as N/A. For example: If 38 items were sold in a quarter hour, each side would need to prep 8 items in order to get 100%.(38 * 0.2 = 7.6 rounded up to 8) If both sides do not prep at least 8 items, it would show 0%. For the full day average, it only counts the 0% and 100% quarter hours since the N/A quarter hours did not have enough items to meet the threshold. Added info: Just a quick recap for future reference - if side 2 is open when it does not need to be, or not open when it should be, it will lower your percentage. A good ratio when it should be open and operational is 1:1 or 2:1. If you open the 2nd side at least once we determine that you have a 2nd side. An "N/A" in this field indicates that there were no quarter hours during the daypart shown when the 2nd side of the Prep Line was required to be open

keyArticles.title: Inventory Analysis Report
keyArticles.body: This report provides multiple topics to evaluate for opportunities to improve inventory. Note: The Mobile Inventory App provides Analysis reporting for all topics that can be checked or corrected using the app. Where do I begin? QSRSoft recommends starting with the topics that have the most items listed. Hover over the "?" to view the recommended action. Inventory Analysis Report General Information Selecting the Information to Display The Class dropdown menu is used to limit the report by product class. Choose a Start Date and End Date . Then click the refresh button to update the table. Various options are provided for viewing the categories where there may be opportunities to improve. Clicking on an individual line will expand only that section, while using the Expand All checkbox button will show or hide all the categories. Clicking on any line will expand that topic to view the items. Hover over each to view recommendations for actions on a topic. Use the refresh icon to display new results after changing the filters at the top. Categories 1-21 1. Items with a large inventory variance over the date range: Recommended Action Review the following item's Raw Item Information to identify the reason for a large change in variance. Managers may be counting the unit of measure differently (i.e. bags vs pounds) Poor timing of counting inventory. For example, items delivered should not be counted until purchases or transfers into the store have been approved. 2. Items not counted over the date range: Recommended Action Please count and submit these items. Not counting items will result in a dramatic increase in stat loss. Stat loss can be viewed on the Variance Stat/Yields page after a physical inventory count has been submitted. 3. Items not in any recipe but with an inventory greater than zero: Recommended Action Put in zero inventory if WRIN is not needed, use "Need Help?" link to open a support ticket if WRIN Should be in a recipe. If the WRIN indicated is in a recipe, open a Support ticket to notify the Support Team. For WRINs no longer in the restaurant submit a zero inventory on the Physical Inventory page. For WRINs with expired product we recommend wasting all inventory on hand so the inventory goes down to zero. Possible reasons for these errors: This may be a legacy product (i.e. no longer used) and that inventory never reached zero. This is a new raw item that has not been included in a recipe. 4. Items with negative actual usage over the date range: Recommended Action Review Raw Item Information and Activity for these items and re-count if necessary. Remember, if you end up with more product than you started with this creates negative actual usage and unexplained difference. Typically, negative actual usage means missing purchases, transfers and inaccurate inventory counts. 5. Items with inventory on multiple WRIN suffixes: Recommended Action Recount WRIN and put zero inventory under unused WRIN. Count the WRIN and enter zero inventory if the Raw Item is no longer in stock. An item has been updated to a new WRIN. However, the inventory did not drop to zero for the old WRIN. Important Note: All duplicate WRINs change recipes after the new WRIN is delivered at the next POS Open. So, all duplicate WRINs must be counted down to zero in the inventory. 6. Items that are not active but are part of an Active Recipe: Recommended Action Contact DC to restrict items not used to fix unexplained differences, also check for correct RFM Menu Items assigned to the restaurant or needing to be deactivated. Determine if the Menu Items that have been assigned by RFM to the restaurant. If the Menu Items are not being sold, have the RFM administrator deactivate them. Determine if the Menu Item is using the Raw Item WRIN shown. If not, contact the DC and have the WRIN restricted. To determine if a Menu Item is using the Raw Item WRIN shown: Click on the Recipe bar to expand it and show the Raw Items in the recipe. 7. Menu items that may have incomplete Recipes: Recommended Action Use the "Need Help?" link to open a support ticket if you are currently selling one of these items. Click Support Chat link in the left-hand menu to let Support know if you are currently selling one of these items. QsrSoft actively looks for incomplete recipes. Occasionally, your restaurant may start selling a Menu Item before the recipe's effective date. Be aware that New Products, Bundles, and Menu Items to be sold soon may have this issue. 8. Purchases auto-approved over the date range entered: Recommended Action To prevent inventory errors, managers should always manually approve purchases. To prevent inventory errors, the manager should always manually approve purchases when the delivery is verified and the product is put away. Customize the Start and End Date(s) to locate Auto Approved Purchases/Invoices on the Purchase page -> History tab Resolve conflicting inventory by clicking on the menu to Chat with Support or open a ticket. 9. Transfers auto-approved over the date range entered: Recommended Action To prevent inventory errors, manager at the Transfer IN restaurant should always manually approve Transfers. We recommend approving Transfers at the time the product is received and always before counting this inventory. 10. Over the date range entered, the top five items transferred IN: Recommended Action Please review ordering processes for these products. If transferring a lot of product IN adjust ordering up and order more product because you are ordering too little. 11. Over the date range entered, the top 5 items transferred OUT: Recommended Action Please review ordering processes for these products. If transferring a lot of product OUT adjust ordering down and order less product because you are ordering too much. 12. Over the date range entered, these dates had zero waste counts: Recommended Action Please follow up with floor managers' process to record waste for these items. 13. Over the date range entered, these dates had less than 50% waste: Recommended Action Please follow up with these shift managers to see if Waste Sheets exist. Add the waste to today and re-inventory. 14. Over the date range entered, these items had the greatest variance: Recommended Action Please review Raw Item Information for these WRINs. Take a new inventory for these WRINs for accuracy. 15. Items that have become obsolete: Recommended Action These WRINs are Obsolete and past the quality date. Please submit a zero inventory for the Obsolete WRINs. If the inventory belongs to another number, update that WRIN's inventory count. Enter the obsolete WRINs as “Waste” and discard product. Deactivate the old WRIN. 16. FOB Projection Status Recommended Action The restaurant did not complete the Food Over Base projections during the time from the 20th to the EOM. Please ask an Above Store User to use the "Edit/Update" button to fill in the missing FOB projections in the Projection tab. The ability to do this is based on user role and permissions. Users without the permission to update projections must contact QsrSoft Support and enter a Support Ticket. Use the Support Chat menu item to reach the Support Team. Note: if projections were completed, the message states: “The restaurant submitted a projection.” 17. Items that have been removed from inventory and have been automatically deactivated. Recommended Action These WRINs were automatically deactivated due to inactivity. There is a 10-day countdown for WRINs that will be automatically deactivated and removed from inventory due to code date expiration. 18. Menu Items being sold that are not active. Recommended Action These are menu items on the POS but have not been authorized for sale in your store. Contact your Field Office to resolve the issue. 19. WRIN usage from a zero priced Menu Item: Recommended Action The WRIN is receiving usage from a zero-priced menu item. Check the Menu Item date range for the menu item number and validate the usage on that date. 20. Invalid substitution key price. Recommended Action These "80-million" numbered items are not the correct keys for pricing substitutions. Please contact your local RFM support for the correct menu item numbers. 21. Items received from the Distribution Center but are not in Cash & Inventory. Recommended Action Contact your Distribution Center and inform them of the items on the invoice that are not Active in MyQSRSoft Inventory for the restaurant.

keyArticles.title: On Hand Inventory
keyArticles.body: The On Hand Inventory report displays the estimated inventory in a restaurant. The filters at the top of the page modify the table. Choose the date needed. The item filter narrows the results in the table. Begin typing the WRIN or item description. Matching WRINs will appear in the table. To view all WRINs again, remove the information from the Item box. It is a best practice to take an inventory for WRINs with negative or zero On Hand amounts to verify that the On Hand Amounts are accurate. The word "(New)" has been added next to the description to help identify the new WRINs and those that need to be removed. New - WRINs that have been in the system for 10 days or less Obsolete - This tag is determined by the last purchase date and shelf life Check the box next to "View ONLY duplicate Prefix WRINs,". Verify which WRINs should be sold and which should be phased out or removed. Check the box next to "View duplicate wrins,". Verify which WRINs should be sold and which should be phased out or removed. What Makes a WRIN Obsolete? An Obsolete WRIN is defined as any WRIN that has its most recent delivery date or transfer date into any given restaurant exceed the number of days of that WRINs Shelf Life. For example, if a WRIN has a shelf life of 30 days and the last time that the restaurant received a delivery of that WRIN was 31 days ago, that WRIN will be considered Obsolete and will be tagged as such. Obsolete WRINs are past the quality date. Please submit a zero inventory for the Obsolete WRINs. If the inventory belongs to another number, update that WRIN's inventory count. Enter the obsolete WRINs as “Waste” and discard product. Deactivate the old WRIN.

keyArticles.title: Physical Inventory
keyArticles.body: Before taking inventory, a message appears. Read then click OK. Items to Inventory Let's explore the Items to Inventory section 1. The ITEMS TO INVENTORY tab opens by default. 2. Message describing items needing to be submitted by date. 3. Select a Count Frequency from the dropdown. Search for a specific item by WRIN or description. 4. Use the Temperature dropdown to view items on the table located in specific areas. 5. Filter table content by Class. 6. Filter the table by range indicator color of inventory submitted. 7. Click the box to view duplicate WRINs. 8. Once counts have been entered, click to Submit All Items. 9. Use this icon to minimize the filter area. Table Data & Function Let's look at the Month-End table view. The table is sorted by Count Saved descending, by default. You can sort by any column. Also, note that you can now view the last time an item count was submitted on the Last Submitted column. To begin taking inventory click on the first item. In this example we are using Apple Drink. Type the amounts in the corresponding boxes, i.e. Case and Each. (The packaging changes depending on the product.) To Add the count, click SAVE. Note: If you are replacing a previous count click the radio button in front of Replace Count before clicking SAVE. When you click save a few things happen. 1. The SUBMIT ALL ITEMS(1) button becomes active and ( ) has a number (1). 2. The Range Indicator color appears providing feedback on the amount expected by the system compared to what was submitted. 3. The next item opens so a count may be entered. When you hit SUBMIT ALL ITEMS(x) The range indicator color turns grey, and the Last Submitted column displays the date and time of the submission. Inventory History Inventory History Let's look at the data under the Inventory History tab to view counted and submitted inventory. Notice the table is sorted by WRIN ascending, by default. Sort by any column by clicking the column title. Users with permissions may edit inventory quantity. Click the Edit icon and retype in the fields. Click the Save icon when done. INVENTORY HISTORY Click the Inventory History tab to view counted and submitted inventory. Search for a specific item Search by Class By default the table is sorted by WRIN. It can be sorted by the other columns. The share icon is available for Premium members only and allows you to share tables with markup directly in QSRSoft Chat. Use the download icon to save the table as an Excel or csv file and to print.

keyArticles.title: QSRSoft Reports - Overview Of Reports
keyArticles.body: Reports Powered By MyQSRSoft provides several categories for viewing your data. Menu Menu Please see the Report Finder Article for information about the Report Finder. Once a specific report is chosen the category and the selection will turn blue. Use the downward chevron/arrow to expand a section and select a report. Narrow the information displayed on each report using Filters. Use the hamburger icon at any time to collapse/show the MyQSRSoft navigation menu. Report Finder Report Finder Please see the Report Finder Article for information about the Report Finder. Business Unit Business Unit Please see the Business Unit Analytics Article for information about Business Unit reporting. This menu item will not appear unless your organization has subscribed to Business Unit Analytics. Cash Cash Sheet The Cash Sheet is an audit of all the cash in and out of the business for the selected date range and group of restaurants. Penny rounding has been added to the Deposit>Expected Cash section and the Cash Sheet Download. In "Additional Info" Tax Exempt Sales is linked to the Tax Exempt Report. Cash Statistics Use this report to follow up on cash controls at the store level. Deposits The Summary tab report displays the sum of deposits for a day or date range and can be grouped by store or by date. The details tab displays individual deposits and details around who bagged, banked, and validated the deposits. Tax Details This Tax Details report contains detailed information about Tax and Tax Chain collections. Tax Exempt This Tax Exempt report contains detailed information about tax-exempt items include a total row. Tax Exempt Sales has been added in Additional Info. A Today tab has been added to this report. Other Receipts The Other Receipts report contains information about payments that happen outside the register system. An example may be the purchase of a newspaper (sales are passed to newspaper vendors but are not part of the store sales). A Today tab has been added to this report. Register Audit Summary of various cash control measures with drill-down to the drawer level. This report has been enhanced to show Security information for Security subscribers in the table. A Drawer Count column has been added. Scroll to the right to see more data. Cashless Report The report contains 3 tabs - Summary, Detail and Mobile. The Summary tab includes a Summary table of cashless transactions. Below that is a table of the cashless transactions by store. The Detail table may only be sorted by Today and Yesterday and include details for transaction-level details of various card types. Click the Mobile tab to view cashless transactions that occurred using a mobile device. Adyen There are 4 tabs to use when examining Adyen data: Adjustment, Variance Summary, Variance Detail, and Payout Summary. Adjustments reports cancellation transaction amounts by start date and end date. Variance Summary provides a summary by date range of transactions processed through Adyen with highlighting to help find differences between the POS and Adyen data. Variance Detail displays all transactions processed through Adyen for a date range. The grid can be sorted and filtered to find transactions in states other than "Settled". And the Payout Summary page reports the totals for batches of Adyen transactions that can be reconciled with bank deposits. Food Inventory There are three tabs to use to view/track your inventory: Ending, On Hand, and Statistics. The Ending Inventory provides inventory totals. Data may also be viewed as a chart. The On Hand tab, which opens when a store number is clicked in the Ending Report table, displays the on-hand inventory data for the selected date, including WRIN, Description, and Inventory Total Cost. Inventory Stat compares expected usage verses actual usage. This report is the Inventory Statistical Loss report and is a comparison between expected usage and actual usage. Transfers This report details product information transferred in or out of another restaurant. Food Over Base The Food Over Base report contains information about controllable food cost contributors such as Raw and Completed Waste, Condiments, Employee and Manager Meals, Variance Stat, and Unexplained. The column Avg Days on Hand Inv is useful to s ee if managers are over ordering, track the b onus program based on food cost, provide indications of stealing, reduce store/org overhead, and help solve a waste problem. Raw Item Count The goal of the Raw Item Count Report is to provide users with the ability to see what stores are taking inventory and at what level they're completing their counts. Using this information, the users can take corrective actions with stores including getting them to take inventory, teaching them which items need to be counted, and setting up locations, etc. The report answers the question: "Are Restaurant Managers following food cost processes and counting the key daily, weekly, and monthly raw items? The report shows the completion of inventory counts for a date or date range. The number of items that were counted is compared to the list of items that are assigned to be counted daily, weekly, and monthly. All inventory items are already on a daily, weekly, or monthly list. Weekly items could be counted a day early depending on Store Settings>Physical Inventory Settings in Cash and Inventory, and monthly items could be counted in the last 3 days of the month depending on Store Settings. Click HERE for more details about this report. Raw Waste Use the tabs at the top to view The Raw Waste Summary, Details, and Today's quantities. Users may click a store number to view details for the store. Completed Waste Use the tabs at the top to view The Completed Waste Summary, Details, and Today's quantities. Users may click a store number to view details for the store. Labor All Hours This report can be used as the Labor Analysis report, the All Hours Pre Review, or the All Hours Post Review depending on how the selectors are chosen and which metrics are displayed. Labor Statistics This report contains a variety of Labor Reporting data along with some sales data. Both Punched Labor and Salaried Labor are available. Labor Schedules This is a simple list of all scheduled shifts: employee and start and end times. Users with PII access are able to view and sort by last names. Social security numbers also display in this report. Labor Analysis The Labor Analysis report shows labor by day or date range with different options for calculating needed hours. Schedule Analysis Summary The Schedule Analysis Summary is a summary of variable, fixed, and floor hours as they are scheduled. This is the report that helps you see what labor % is scheduled and whether you are correctly assigning the needed hours for the projected sales and guest counts. Use this report after schedules are complete but before the schedule period arrives so that you catch problems and correct them. Schedule Variance The Schedule Variance This report focuses on Variable Labor Hours and gives you the overall hours short or over, as well as the variance. Variance means hours plus or minus added together. For example, if I was one hour short of VLH need for the lunch rush, and one hour more than VLH need for the dinner rush, that would be 2 hours of variance. A schedule that has low VLH +/- but high Variance is a schedule where the hours are not carefully scheduled to the business needs throughout the day. VLH Report Review overall Variable Labor Hours or individual VLH stations throughout the scheduled day to ensure that you have scheduled appropriately for the projected transactions. This report is located under ReportsLaborVLH Over/Under (Labor Area) VLH Over Under is its own report but is also the drill-down from the Schedule Variance Report. The table is folded by default but can be expanded. The folded view shows the totals. Expanded View shows qtr hr detail only (no option for full hours). Use the VLH over/under report to see how VLH hours are scheduled through the day to see where you are scheduled over and under need. Digital At A Glance This report provides information specific to the Mobile App. Digital App Charts The first chart provides an average guest count breakdown By Store. Toggle By Date to view the chart organized by a selected date or date range. Hover over any part of the chart or the legend at the bottom to focus on specific areas of the chart. Click the gear icon at the top right of each report to change how the data is viewed. Other charts included are: Loyalty GC Breakdown MOP Fulfillment Breakdown Digital App P&L Breakdown There is also a Digital App table in this section. Understanding the Loyalty GC Breakdown Chart When customers are earning or redeeming mobile points it shows up in this area Loyalty transaction Breakdown Loyalty Earn No Reward % of Total GC The customer earned points on the transaction but redeemed no points. Loyalty Rewards Only % of Total GC The customer only redeemed points, no points were earned. Loyalty Rewards & Earned % of Total GC The customer earned some points and burned some points. MOP Fulfillment Breakdown These are all Mobile Order and Pay Transactions that show where the order was picked up MOP GCs Fulfilled at Curbside MOP GCs Fulfilled at Table Service MOP GCs Fulfilled at FC (Front Counter) MOP GCs Fulfilled at DT (Drive Thru) Click the gear icon to choose between Guest Counts and Guest Count %. This is a percent of MOP guest counts. Digital App P&L Breakdown This report shows a side-by-side view of sales and costs from transactions associated with the Digital App. This report can be customized by clicking the gear icon and choosing one option from the pop up box. Costs are broken down by: Reward Promo F&P Reduction – Most Loyalty Rewards will be a promo where a customer receives an item at no charge. The entire food and paper cost for the free item are included. Reward Disc F&P Reduction - Note that the majority of rewards will fall into promo. The only time a Loyalty Reward will show under discount is if a customer is charged for any type of customization to their reward. When they are charged for the customization, that transaction is categorized as a discount. This is most common in transactions that include a kid's meal reward. The food and paper cost reflect the discounted portion of the item only. For example, if an item is discounted 50%, then 50% of the food and paper cost for the item will be included. Offer Promo F&P Reduction – These are standard “free” GMA offers (ex. Buy one Breakfast Sandwich, Get one Free). The entire food and paper cost dollars for the free item are included. Offer Discount F&P Reduction – These are standard discounted GMA offers (ex. $1 Large Fries, $3 off any Purchase of $15 or more). The food and paper cost reflect the discounted portion of the item only. Digital App Sales Clicking the launch button opens the Mobile P&L Detail report which has filters to use to customize the report. To view At A Glance rankings between selected locations click the icon on each container. There is a Digital Snapshot area on the Home page also. At the top right of the page, click the gear icon to determine which containers to show and in what order they appear. Digital App The Digital App Report contains anything associated with the Digital App - loyalty, MOP, and scanned offers. Digital Usage The Digital Usage Report contains anything associated with the Digital App, loyalty, MOP, and scanned offers plus Kiosk and 3PO. Basically any orders that are digital. Mobile Offer List This report displays information about offers redeemed through the Mobile App. Some of those offers are applied to orders entered in the app, and others are applied to orders entered through the POS system. Personalized Offers (National Test) leverage the Pricing Engine 3.0 (PE3) Digital Offers Engine —a smart system that uses customer and market data to generate more relevant, personalized offers aimed at driving profitable growth across the system. Currently, McDonald’s is in a testing phase, targeting 10% of customers nationally in every restaurant. The test applies to always-on segmented and local offers, all of which have been approved by the Digital Value Team . Given the volume and complexity of personalized offers recommended by PE3, we’ve consolidated the data into a single row per restaurant . This approach allows for more meaningful, interpretable reporting while ensuring all offers remain within the segmented offer bank guardrails as approved by OPNAD . Mobile P&L Detail This report provides details about the promos and discounts that are part of Mobile Orders. GMA Delivery This report provides details about Global Mobile App (GMA) individual transactions. This report details McDonalds Integrated delivery for orders through the mobile app and sent to a 3rd party vendor for fulfillment. Options are available to roll up or down to the quarter hour level by daypart. National Employee Discount (NED) The National Employee Discount and the NED By Employee reports have been consolidated. Use the tab at the top of the page to view each report. The National Employee Discount and the NED By Employee report displays sales from this program by employee. Product Delivery Price Index Delivery Price Index is a quick list of system-wide top selling delivery menu items, with delivery price, non-delivery price, and delivery premium %. Use it to get a quick gauge on your overall Delivery premium. RFM Price Comparison This report is used to compare menu prices between stores or use as a price list if only one store is selected. Product Mix Use the tabs at the top to view PMIX in multiple ways (PMIX, PMIX LIVE, and MGR/EMP MEALS). All of these reports provide Product Mix exactly as recorded by the Cash and Inventory Application. View multiple locations, individual locations or all locations combined Select Watch Lists or Menu Items View Delivery and Non-Delivery together or separately using the Point Of Order selector In addition the PMIX & MGR/EMP MEALS reports provide PMIX first by Time Segment: Day, Dayparts, Peaks. Next View Segment By Total, By Hour, By Quarter Hour, By Daypart. Choose Time Segment Select Dayparts View Segment By Select By Hour or By Quarter Hour To view by PEAK Choose Time Segment Select Peaks from the dropdown. Choose Peaks Use the dropdown under Peaks to select all, multiple or a single peak time. PMIX Discount This report provides Discount Menu Items by Discount event, a detail of all associated discounted menu items. View Menu Items from multiple locations, individual locations or all locations combined View Menu Items by a single Point of Order or all Points of Order combined View single menu items or a Watchlist $0 priced items now supported Product Mix Trend This report allows for up to 5 Menu Items and displays date range trends by Date, Week or Month. The Product Mix Trend Report provide highly flexible views of product mix details. View one location or a consolidation of all locations, view a single date or a date range. The data can be narrowed using the Point of Order selector. Point Of Order Defined Front Counter = Front Counter Register Transactions including Delivery and MOP attended, unattended and curbside transactions In Store = Front Counter Transactions + Kiosk Transactions Delivery = Delivery Transactions MOP = MOP Transaction including curbside, drive thru, attended and unattended Drive Thru = Drive Thru Transactions including MOP drive thru transactions Combined = In Store + Drive Thru (all transactions) Reported Product Outage The Reported Product Outage report shows items that have been marked deactivated on the POS at the restaurant. Kitchen Capacity Report The Kitchen Capacity Report shows units sold at the restaurant. People At A Glance The People At A Glance Dashboard provides a quick view of statistics related to Crew and Managers. Overview Settings Click the gear icon to select which metrics to display in each of the containers and which containers to display. This area defaults to the last completed month 1. Hover over the to view the meaning of the colors in the containers. 2. Click the tabs to view additional data. Container Specific Tips Staffing Active employees - not terminated and worked some hours Inactive employees- not terminated but did not have any hours Time & Attendance 3 minutes late is considered late in the Overview (if the user selected On Time Rating in the cogs icon) Shift If the actual hours is quite a bit less than the needed hours, the numbers will be red and could indicate that the service being provided is not the best If the location used more hours than were actually needed, the number could be over 100% Turnover & Retention This is annualized over the last 12 months. The monthly turnover is multiplied by 12 to make it comparable to an annual number Shift The Shift Report is an expansion of the Shift Section. Looking at the Total will match the At A Glance container. Looking by location can determine if one or several locations are causing the numbers to not be close to the threshold. View actual hours vs what was needed The launch icon will bring up the more detailed Shift Report and table. Turnover Trend The Turnover Trend Charts contain a Monthly Annual Turnover, TTM Turnover, and YTD Turnover. Hover over each line to streamline the view. The launch icon provides additional ways to filter the data. Click Filters to access filter by all locations Click the tabs to update the table. LM - limits table data to information from last month January thru Last Month Trailing 13 Months Calendar - click to customize a Start and End Date. Click to view data for Crew, Swing, and Manager Click the Save icon to save. Use the dropdown arrow to reset all values. Click the Refresh icon to update the data Employee Roster A list of all employees entered in WFM software. Employees with permission can easily view Payroll IDs with other Roster information. Various filters provide views of current roster or historic roster. The Employee Roster report includes the ability to email employees/crew. Checkboxes are at the far left. Put checks in the boxes and click the "Copy Emails" button to copy a string of email addresses separated by commas that you can paste into the "To", "CC", or "BCC" fields of your email program. If you use Outlook, drop the arrow on the button to copy the emails separated by a semicolon. A Payroll ID field is now available to add to the table. Birthdays & Anniversaries The Birthdays and Anniversaries report lists today's and upcoming employee birthdays under the Birthday tab, and Anniversaries and other work milestones for celebration under the Anniversary tab. Roster Statistics This report provides details for people who are active, not active, the number of people on staff for various job title codes, and percentage of minors on staff. “Active” indicates that an employee that had punches in selected month. Turnover This report contains information about the number of terminations compared to staff size for selected month range. 3 Month Turnover Explanation 3 month turnover is a special measure similar to 90-day turnover. For each month, we are looking back in the past for a period of three months where all hires can be known to have made it 90 days or not. For February, the most recent month where all hires are for sure known to have made it 90 days is October. For employees that were hired in November, December, or January, we haven't had a full 90 days elapse yet. So the 3-month period is Aug-Sep-Oct. We add up the total number of hires for those three months. Then we add up the total number of those hires that did not make it to 90 days, and we call that number "3-Month Terms". New hires that did stay for at least 90 days are called "3-Month Retained". "3-Month Turnover" is 3-Month Terms divided by total hires in that 3-month period. Store Time Punches This is a simple list of all time punches by store and employee which includes an "In Modified" column and an "Out Modified" column. Users with PII access are able to view and sort by last names. Social security numbers also display in this report. A new Punch Type of "lactation" has been added and will appear on the Store Time Punches report for states that have that type of paid break. Time Punch Export System Administrators can now use the Time Punch Export feature to export employee time punches to a file. This file can then be delivered via email or printed. The export can also be shared through chat using the quick share icon. Note: A maximum of five (5) employees can be exported at a time. Labor Exceptions The Labor Exceptions report showing a summary and detail of labor rule exceptions as sent to QSRSoft by the workforce management vendor. Time & Attendance This report is designed to provide a view into how well employees do at coming in for work and arriving on time. There are several options for date or date range. Emp Hours this Week This Employee Hours this Week report adds hours already worked from time punches to remaining hours scheduled to estimate total hours the employee will get in the current week to help control overtime. Shift This report is designed to provide a look into Labor Statistics (Actual vs needed across categories) by month. Rewards Use this report to track reward points by location and employee. Use filters to specify date range and see table date BY DATE or SUM. Payroll Employee Time Punches Look up a single employee by the last four digits of their SSN OR search using the employees last name. For names shorter than 4 letters add spaces to reach 4 characters. Helpful when researching punches for various legal claims. New Hires A list of all employees hired since a given date. Date Selector is the last day of completed pay cycles. Pay Period Activity A summary of changes across employees in a given pay period. View active employees with no hours, terminations, Leaves of Absence, and wage and Job Title Code changes. Use the Pay Period Activity report at the end of each pay cycle to identify changes that might need to be addressed as you complete the payroll. Pay Cycle Status A list showing whether a payroll file was received from a WFM vendor for Current, Next, or most recently released pay cycle. Payroll Ledger Provides a summary of hours across the pay period with one row per employee per badge type. Employees who work both primary and secondary jobs will have two rows in the ledger. For detail about hour types, rate and rate changes, and more see Employee Pay Detail Employee Pay Details A detailed break-out of all pay types, hours, and dollars for each employee. One row is provided in the detail for each employee by pay type, wage rate, job title code, or "Lawson Code" (miscellaneous hours category). Overtime Audit The Overtime Audit report is available by pay cycles and it shows overtime and double time hours by employee. Users with PII access are able to view and sort by last names. Social security numbers also display in this report. Employee Hours Look Back Average Weekly Hours for employees across a historical period, typically used to look at hours for the last year to determine if employees qualify for benefits. Student Permit Status Check Report The Student Permit Status Check Report displays expiring student permit documents. This is a replacement for the dotComm report. Sales McDelivery The McDelivery report shows information about delivery orders. Use the McDelivery tab to view such as sales and transactions and includes data from the Third Party delivery vendors such as Orders with Inaccurate or Missing items. A Today tab has been added to this report. McDelivery 3PO This report provides information from McDonalds 3rd party ordering (3PO) vendors - this data is delayed and the earliest date to pick is 4 days ago. This includes info about how long a vendor waits for orders in the parking lot. Kiosk This report provides Kiosk Sales results that can be compared to other Points of Order using the secondary options (Day, Dayparts, Peaks, Timeslices) on the right side of the page. Included is a Cash tab to view Kiosk Cashless and Cash transactions. Sales Ledger This report provides Day results, trend by day, week or month through the date aggregation selector. Consolidated Sales This report is a single report that contains All Net Sales +/- details for different time periods. (day, month to date, year to date, and more) Sales - Point Of Order This report provides resolution down to the Qtr Hr of Sales by various points of order. In-store includes Front Counter & Kiosk Front Counter (FC) includes Front Counter registers, Delivery and MOP (attended, unattended and curbside) Sales Ledger Summary This report provides sales measures at a full day resolution. It provides sales groups Breakfast, Drive Thru, Kiosk, Mobile, Delivery and Total/Storewide. Where Served Sales by "point of delivery". An order that starts on the mobile app and is fulfilled through Drive Thru would be counted as DT sales. Use the Sales - Point of Order report to see sales by order initiation point. Open Late Close Early Shows RFM scheduled Open and Close times for the restaurant overall and for the lobby, and compares those times to the first quarter hour that had sales (Open) or the last quarter hour that had sales (Close) to identify a possible situation where the restaurant opened late or closed early. Store Hours Shows the scheduled open and close times by day as set in RFM. Service Service Time Statistics This report provides various service timing metrics as measured by the POS down to the quarter-hour level. The report includes R2P split between the front counter and kiosk. MOP Service Times This report provides Ready on Arrival (ROA) service times for orders through the app. This has categories for where the customer picked up the order (curbside, drive-thru, FC, etc). TIP: Choosing metrics like curbside, delivery and pull forward are useful to determine if enough people are scheduled at the busiest times of day in these areas. YYNN A report designed to help report on 2 key measures - OEPE and Transaction growth in Drive Thru. Lower Order End to Present End (OEPE) means more transactions can be done for different time periods. If both areas are improving the report will show “YY”, if both not improving the report will show “NN”. “YN” and “NY” are also options. VOICE This report provides information from McDonalds surveys through the VOICE system. This is customer feedback. DT Timer This report is for locations with HME or Acrelec timers in the drive-thru. This report includes Speed Of Service information. Shift 3D Trend This report is used to view data for the 3D's - Digital / Drive Thru / Delivery. One location is chosen and the data is averaged for each hour on the day selected with the same day the last 4 weeks. If several days are chosen the table show each date separately. TIP: Choosing metrics like curbside, delivery, and pull forward are useful to determine if enough people are scheduled at the busiest times of day in these areas. Trends Quickly trend results in different categories by restaurant or across restaurant groups - Sales, Service, and Digital. This report is available to SimpleThink/QSRSoft Premium subscribers. Rank Quickly rank restaurants within a group on sales, service, cash controls, and food cost. Rank is a great tool for comparing restaurants during restaurant manager performance reviews. This report is available to SimpleThink/QSRSoft Premium subscribers. 3 Peaks This report provides sales and service information across McDonalds 3 peaks 7-9am, 11-2pm and 5-7pm. Daily Activity Report (DAR) The Daily Activity Report is a blend of various sales, service, and labor measures down to the quarter hour level. Only one day can be selected. The report will display the hours from 4 AM until 4 AM regardless of when POS Close/Open is completed. TIP: Click on the column headers to sort them and bring the lowest or highest value to the top. You might want to see which location and hour has the highest OEPE, or the greatest difference between Projected Transactions and Actual Transactions. Focus On Service This report helps correlate Labor Hours used with sales and service measures. A single day or a date range can be viewed, but hour and quarter hour views are only available if a single date is selected. Operations Report The Operations Report has 3 sections for Sales information, Service timing, and Controls (which currently includes cash and labor). Each section can be customized and saved separately. The report can be pulled by date or date range. The report allows you to view Last Year's Metrics and Year to Date. Click the gear icon to access column settings and look for LY or YTD. The column displays once selected. Shift Manager Summary This report shows key metrics across managers and shifts. Currently, the GEID of the person is shown, but this will soon be updated to show manager names. If a person runs multiple shifts in the selected date range, that person's shifts will be rolled together to produce an aggregated scorecard. Peak Target and Tracking The Peak Target and Tracking report shows projected transactions for peak periods and tracks actual results against those projections. Find My Peak Search for record hours in various sales, guest count, and service metrics. Find My Peak will always return 4 consecutive quarter hours. Use the Hour/Quarter Hour toggle to return a set of 4 qtr hrs that begin and end on the hour (e.g. 12-1), or cross over between clock hours (e.g. 11:45-12:45). Time Slice Summary A "mini ops report" that allows a focus on specific dayparts including overnight. Daily Glimpse A one-day "operations report" that can be set to be emailed each day to MyQSRSoft users within your organization. Punch Summary The Punched Summary Report provides the user with key metrics about managers at one location while punched in. Not available for salaried managers. The table data may be sent via chat using the icon, and it is downloadable. The data may be used to coach managers by evaluating labor and healthy second-side usage, and more. Note: The Crew tab is only available to QSRSoft Premium Subscribers. Records Report The Records Report was created to identify the best records for an organization, allowing them to strive to beat these records. Clients may now see their yearly best month ever by clicking Yearly, then choose the year from the dropdown. Make selections for Time Frame, Days of the Week, and Best Record Type. Remember to tap the refresh icon to update the table data. Forms Forms Completion Report The Forms Completion Report is available for Premium subscribers to track completed forms by location and date range. System Administrators now have an option for "No Location" on the Forms Completion Report. This will return forms with no locations attached. System Administrators also have an option for selecting Patches on the Forms Completion Report. This will return forms assigned to a Patch of stores. CoachQ automatically provides metrics to analyze the form completion rates on the Completion Details tab. Here is an example: Clicking the CoachQ button will prompt you for further details and make suggestions for improvement.

keyArticles.title: Raw Item Count Report
keyArticles.body: Raw Item Count Report The report shows the completion of inventory counts for a date or date range. The number of items that were counted is compared to the list of items that are assigned to be counted daily, weekly, and monthly. All inventory items are already in a daily, weekly, or monthly list. Weekly items could be counted a day early depending on Store Settings>Physical Inventory Settings in Cash and Inventory, and monthly items could be counted in the last 3 days of the month depending on Store Settings. Let's take a look at the icons on the top right of the table. Opens a legend explaining how the table works. The Column Descriptions tab is described below. Choose which columns you want to show on the table by clicking in the box. Select All is an option. Scroll down to view more. The download file name may be changed. Click the "Include Hidden Columns" box to show all available columns. Click the dropdown to save the file as an Excel or CSV file. The file may also be printed from here. Let's take a look at the tabs along the top of the table. The table default displays the Daily, Weekly, and Monthly counts. Click the Daily tab to only see Daily, the same for Weekly and Monthly. Tips For Using This Report If Store Settings in Cash and Inventory allow items to be counted a day before the weekly count, check both days and add the percentages for the weekly counts. Select "Allow Day before Weekly" in the gear for Column Settings so it is visible. View the number of days for monthly counts to be taken by selecting this column using the gear for Column Settings. Look at all those days to add the percentages for monthly items. The Legend (displayed using the i-icon), explains the colors used in this report for the number of counts taken (<10%, 10%-75%, and >75%) and the type of counts (Daily, Weekly, or Monthly). There is also a tab for COLUMN DESCRIPTIONS as well. These are those descriptions.
